summary: A single on or off choice with its label next to the box, submitted with a form. Supports a mixed state for a parent that controls a partly checked group.

p.label: Notify reviewers when I open a pull request
Require two approvals
p.description: Token changes merge only after a designer and an engineer approve.

whenToUse: An independent yes or no that takes effect when the form is saved: agree, include, require.
Several independent options under one question: put them in a CheckboxGroup.
Selecting rows in a Table (with a parent checkbox in the header for select all).
whenNotToUse: A setting that applies immediately: use Switch.
One choice among exclusive options: use RadioGroup.

dos.title: Phrase the label as the positive case
dos.text: Checked means the label is true. "Notify reviewers" reads cleanly; a negative label makes users double-check.

dos.title: Use the description for consequences
dos.text: Keep the label short and explain the effect underneath.

p.label: Require two approvals
p.description: Token changes merge only after a designer and an engineer approve.

donts.title: Negative labels
donts.text: "Do not send notifications" checked means off. Users have to think twice.

donts.title: A checkbox that acts immediately
donts.text: If ticking it changes something right away, it is a Switch.

accessibility: Base UI Checkbox: role checkbox, Space toggles, aria-checked is true, false or mixed (indeterminate).
The whole label row is the click target; the label text is the accessible name (aria-labelledby) and the description is linked with aria-describedby.
The box edge uses color.border.strong (3:1 against surfaces); checked uses the ink fill with a white check (4.5:1 or more).
Indeterminate shows a dash, so mixed is not conveyed by color.
invalid adds a danger edge; always pair it with an error message in the group or form.
contentGuidelines: Sentence case, no trailing period on the label.
Describe the result of checking it, not the control: "Notify reviewers", not "Check to notify".
